title: hermes-runs-as-a-device-beside-cc
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> [TICKETME:waiting] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(a_suspicion_becomes_a_sieve) -> PROVED
intention: hermes-agent runs as a Cairn DEVICE (instance 0) on this box beside CC — its inference out through the proxy and its own JSONL ledgers tailed into the device's diagnostic trail — so a second agent's thoughts AND its actions are both inspectable without forking it.
why: Law 8 (peers require trust, so prove first — it enters proven-space by grafting, one ticket at a time, and 3,977 upstream tests buy it nothing here); Law 10 (nothing in the system is immeasurable — a second agent is inside that set, not above it); Law 7 (its trail is a record of truth and may never collapse an error); Law 4 (the rule that it cannot red anything must be PHYSICS, not hermes' good manners).
how: A device directory with a charter and instance 0. Its model calls point at the OpenAI-shaped door (sibling intent) so cognition lands in the meter and the trail. Its own ledgers — skill_ledger.jsonl, the curator ledger — are tailed into the device's diagnostic trail through the existing diagnostic.py floor, so ACTION is recorded beside COGNITION. Its declared role is peer and antagonist: it files questions and troubles, and passes no gate, ever.
falsifier: DONE when hermes runs on this box; every model call it makes appears in inference_calls; every skill or memory mutation it makes appears in the device's trail; and it has filed at least one trouble or question that CC did not raise. WRONG INTENT if keeping it inspectable turns out to require forking it after all (the fork was the option this design exists to avoid), or if the antagonist produces suspicions nobody ever converts into a sieve — a peer whose findings never become physics is a second opinion, not a second party. MEASURED CONSTRAINT that may relocate rather than kill it: this box has 15GB total and ~9GB available, and CC has OOM-killed it three times at 12-14GB; if two agents cannot coexist here the device moves to Hex and the intent survives at a different address.
traces_to: Law 8 (peers require trust, so prove first — it enters proven-space by grafting, one ticket at a time, and 3,977 upstream tests buy it nothing here); Law 10 (nothing in the system is immeasurable — a second agent is inside that set, not above it); Law 7 (its trail is a record of truth and may never collapse an error); Law 4 (the rule that it cannot red anything must be PHYSICS, not hermes' good manners).

watchme.trigger: each trouble or question filed by the hermes device
watchme.enough: when 20 hermes-filed suspicions have been dispositioned — at that point the conversion rate to a deterministic sieve that actually fired is a measured number and the antagonist either pays for its RAM or does not
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier clause: at least one filed trouble or question CC did not raise, and the fraction of filed suspicions that became sieves
watchme.nexus: the trouble store plus the question corpus — the two places a suspicion can land, so the probe reads what exists rather than a new table
watchme.consumer: Akien, because whether a second agent earns its keep is a spec question his head settles, not a measurement-settled one

gates_bound: proof gate — proofs beside the code, run by the tester under netns isolation; teeth a hollow build could not pass (Law 8).
feeds back to origin on failure — a red routes to this ticket's own voyage, never to a paragraph (Law 3 + the deterministic-red rule: fixed, or carrying a ruling from Akien).
durability gate — not done until proven AND committed.

emit chokepoint — every crossing rides cairn.tools.base.transitions.emit at the component's own address carrying this ticket id; BUILDME refused without a berthed validate packet claiming it, PROVED refused without a complete passing verdict artifact.
owner: CC builds it; the hermes device owns its own instance state once it stands. Akien owns the design ratification — whether a second agent runs here at all is a spec question, not a measurement-settled one
owning_intention: cairn/devices/hermes/intention+why.json — TO BE WRITTEN BY THIS TICKET; the device does not exist yet
depends_on: QUEUED ON the OpenAI-door ticket (548dd13fb4db) (sibling, same idea). hermes' inference has nowhere metered to go until that door stands, and running it un-metered even once would make its first calls the only ones this system cannot see.
children: none yet, but ONE IS LIKELY: if hermes may not fire the trouble and question doors directly (the open Law 6 edge in missing_check), an admission path becomes a child ticket. It is not cast now because the edge is a question, not a settled design.
